rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure across the board: the program is tiny (600 bytes of text, 47 mostly small functions), so size overhead is cheap and BCF/FLA/SUB are pushed hard to swell and tangle the few large bodies (main, pop_around::cycle, simulation_unit::mov). SPLIT gets high diversity/size weights since fragmenting small functions compounds the effect of the other passes cheaply, and IBR is kept high to obscure the control-flow edges FLA/BCF create. ICALL and IGV are raised moderately from a conservative round-1 baseline but with the lowest CorrectnessRisk weights, because this is a C++ program with constructors and indirect-call-prone semantics (vtables, runtime dispatch) where aggressive indirect-call rewriting and global variable merging carry the most correctness exposure; keeping their risk tolerance below 0.5 lets the feature-driven selector apply them only where features clearly favor it, preserving the round-1 correctness result while still adding symbol/reference-level obfuscation.
